item.title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
item.description: arXiv:2610.41233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component. This domain-dependent sign contradicts the uniform crossing relations of the HOMFLYPT skein algebra. We show that this discrepancy is resolved by passing to an anti-holomorphic orientation convention. We establish all required orientation comparisons in the general setting of an oriented Lagrangian submanifold of a 6-dimensional symplectic manifold.
item.dc:creator: Brett Parker

item.title: The Berger conjecture for three dimensional manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.41006v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A conjecture of Berger says that on a simply connected manifold all of whose geodesics are closed, all unit speed geodesics have the same shortest period. In this paper we will show that the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow is free. We use symplectic geometry to investigate the topology of the quotient of the unit tangent bundle T^1M/S^1 by the S^1 action that comes from the geodesic flow. We show that this quotient admits the structure of a smooth symplectic manifold and that this symplectic manifold is symplectomorphic to S^2 \times S^2 equipped with a split form. This will enable a computation involving the Euler class of the orbibundle T^1M\rightarrow T^1M/S^1 which will lead to a solution of Berger's conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Dittmer

item.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
item.description: arXiv:2610.41635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Although nonconservative forces and extended phase space are individually common topics in Hamiltonian dynamics, their combination is seldom developed explicitly. This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion for nonconservative and nonautonomous dynamical systems formulated on extended phase space. Particular attention is given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. The classic analytical dynamics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates (i.e., canonical coordinates) or functions thereof.
item.dc:creator: Joseph T. A Peterson, Manoranjan Majji, John L. Junkins

item.title: Constructing Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from multi-grid diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2610.42076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a new diagrammatic construction of Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from objects called multi-grid diagrams. These are a generalisation of triple grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ wherein the underlying trisection is replaced by the more general notion of a toric decomposition. We give examples of multi-grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in a range of symplectic toric $4$-manifolds, including Evans' recent non-squeezable Klein bottle in $S^2 \times S^2$.
item.dc:creator: Shintaro Fushida-Hardy, Laura Wakelin

item.title: Abelianization and moment maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.42123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$. We do this by looking at the restriction of $\mu$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.
item.dc:creator: Elana Kalashnikov, Ruxandra Moraru, Francisco Villacis
